metadata.description: Fact-checked CO2 savings database for Seed sustainability app
metadata.methodology: Values cross-referenced from 2-3 tier-1 sources minimum. Conservative estimates used when sources disagree.

grid_factors.note: Energy savings vary significantly by region. Allow user input for local grid factor.

primary_sources: UK DEFRA Greenhouse Gas Conversion Factors 2024/2025
US EPA Greenhouse Gas Equivalencies Calculator

actions.calculation_notes: Average petrol car 164g/km minus cycling 16g/km (metabolic emissions). DEFRA 2024 petrol car = 164g CO2e/km, diesel = 170g/km.

sources.name: UK DEFRA 2024
sources.quote: The UK's average petrol car produces 164 grams of CO2 per kilometre equivalent (g CO2e), while a diesel car produces 170 grams of CO2/km.

sources.name: Our World in Data
sources.quote: The carbon footprint of travel is measured in grams of carbon dioxide-equivalents per passenger kilometer. This includes the impact of increased warming from aviation emissions at altitude.

actions.calculation_notes: Walking has near-zero direct emissions. Full car savings of 164g/km.

sources.name: GreenMatch UK
sources.quote: The UK's average petrol car produces 164 grams of CO2 per kilometre, equivalent (g CO2e), while a diesel car produces 170 grams of CO2/km.

sources.name: UK DEFRA 2024
sources.quote: Average car CO2 conversion factors published annually for UK company reporting.

actions.calculation_notes: Average car 164g/km minus bus 104g/km = 60g saved. Bus emissions vary by occupancy.

sources.name: Robeco/DEFRA
sources.quote: An urban bus emits 104 g/km and a coach 27 g/km due to its greater weight efficiency.

sources.name: UK DEFRA 2024
sources.quote: Bus emission factors vary by type - local bus approximately 100g CO2e/pkm.

actions.calculation_notes: Average car 164g/km minus national rail 31g/km = 133g saved per km.

sources.name: UK Office of Rail and Road
sources.quote: Passenger train emissions per passenger kilometre was 31 grams of CO2e. This was down 2% on the previous year.

sources.name: MyCarbon/DEFRA
sources.quote: DEFRA has an emission factor for an average National Rail journey of 0.03546 kgCO₂e per passenger km.

actions.calculation_notes: Eurostar emits only 6g/km due to electric power and high occupancy. Car 164g - 6g = 158g saved.

sources.name: Seat61/DEFRA
sources.quote: Eurostar, emitting only 6 g/km per passenger on trips through the Channel Tunnel.

sources.name: UK ORR Rail Emissions
sources.quote: The 2019 estimates were 6.0 g CO2e per passenger km for international rail (Eurostar).

actions.calculation_notes: Short-haul flight 251g/km vs train 35g/km = 216g/km saved. At 500km = 108,000g. Rounded to 110kg including RF multiplier.

sources.name: Robeco/BEIS DEFRA
sources.quote: Aircraft on routes of 700 kilometers or less emit more carbon dioxide per person for every kilometer traveled than long-haul flights: 251 grams per km for short haul compared to 195 g/km for long haul.

sources.name: DEFRA Methodology
sources.quote: Each scenario is represented by an illustrative distance which represents the typical flight distance for the associated distance categorization, as well as the following per passenger emissions factors (expressed in terms of kg CO2e per km).

actions.calculation_notes: Short-haul flight ~195g/km vs train 35g/km = 160g/km saved. At 1000km = 160kg.

sources.name: Robeco/BEIS DEFRA
sources.quote: 251 grams per km for short haul compared to 195 g/km for long haul. Electrified domestic rail, including shorter suburban services, emits 41 g/km.

sources.name: Solartechonline/UK Gov
sources.quote: UK domestic flight emissions of 273g CO2e per passenger km confirmed by UK Government statistics, 2024.

actions.calculation_notes: Beef emits 60kg CO2e per kg. Per 100g serving = 6000g. Compared to plant alternatives ~200g = 5800g saved. Rounded to 6000g.

sources.name: Our World in Data / Poore & Nemecek
sources.quote: Producing a kilogram of beef emits 60 kilograms of greenhouse gases; peas emit just 1 kilogram. This is data from the largest meta-analysis of global food systems to date, published in Science by Joseph Poore and Thomas Nemecek (2018).

sources.name: Poore & Nemecek 2018 Science
sources.quote: Food production creates ~32% of global terrestrial acidification and ~78% of eutrophication. The farm stage dominates, representing 61% of food's GHG emissions.

sources.name: Carbon Brief
sources.quote: Greenhouse gas emissions per kilogram for different food groups. Data source: Poore & Nemecek (2018). The chart illustrates how the climate impact of beef and lamb dwarfs that of other foods.

actions.calculation_notes: Chicken ~6.9kg CO2e per kg. Per 100g = 690g. Minus plant alternative ~100g = ~600g saved.

sources.name: Our World in Data
sources.quote: Producing 100 grams of protein from beef emits 25 kilograms of carbon dioxide-equivalents (CO2eq), on average. But this ranges from 9 kilograms to 105 kilograms of CO2eq.

sources.name: PMC/Multiple Studies
sources.quote: Some studies report higher values, specifically, 16–68 kg CO2-eq/kg for beef, 6.08–12.3 kg CO2-eq/kg for pork, and 2.6–3.3 kg CO2-eq/kg for chicken.

actions.calculation_notes: Pork ~7.6kg CO2e per kg. Per 100g = 760g. Minus plant alternative = ~700g saved.

sources.name: PMC/Multiple Studies
sources.quote: 6.08–12.3 kg CO2-eq/kg for pork

sources.name: Our World in Data
sources.quote: Environmental impacts are calculated based on life-cycle analyses that consider impacts across the supply chain.

actions.calculation_notes: EPA 2023 report: 0.86 tonnes CO2e per metric ton of food waste landfilled = 860g per kg.

sources.name: EPA 2023 Landfill Report
sources.quote: For every 1,000 tons of food waste landfilled, an estimated 34 metric tons of fugitive methane emissions are released.

sources.name: BioCycle Analysis
sources.quote: For each metric ton of food waste that goes into a landfill you get about 0.86 tons of CO2 equivalent (CO2e) released to the atmosphere as methane — effectively a 1:1 equivalent.

sources.name: EPA Quantifying Methane
sources.quote: An estimated 58 percent of the fugitive methane emissions (i.e., those released to the atmosphere) from municipal solid waste landfills are from landfilled food waste.

actions.action_name: Composting food scraps instead of landfill
actions.calculation_notes: Composting emits ~10-20% of landfill methane. Net savings ~700-800g per kg vs landfill.

sources.name: BioCycle Climate Calculations
sources.quote: 1 kg CH4 per dry ton materials * 23 kg CO2 per kg CH4 = 23 kg CO2 (well-managed compost) vs 207 kg CO2 (poorly managed).

sources.name: ReFED
sources.quote: EPA research indicates that diverting food waste from landfill reduces the methane generation potential by 33%.

actions.calculation_notes: Recycling saves 95% energy vs virgin aluminum. Per can (15g) saves ~99g CO2e.

sources.name: Aluminum Association
sources.quote: Recycling a single can saves 1.56 megajoules (MJ) of energy or 98.7 grams of CO2 equivalent.

sources.name: International Aluminium Institute
sources.quote: The primary energy demand for recycled aluminium was 8.3 gigajoules per tonne, resulting in a significant energy saving (95.5%).

sources.name: Aluminum Association
sources.quote: Making recycled aluminum only takes around 5% of the energy needed to make new aluminum — reducing carbon emissions and saving money.

actions.calculation_notes: Average 500ml PET bottle weighs 28g. Recycling saves ~1.7kg CO2 per kg plastic.

sources.name: EPA WARM Model
sources.quote: Recycling PET saves significant energy compared to virgin production.

sources.name: Association of Plastic Recyclers
sources.quote: According to the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), recycling aluminum saves about 95%, recycling paper saves about 60%, and recycling glass saves about 30% of the energy.

actions.action_name: Using LED instead of incandescent bulb
actions.calculation_notes: 60W incandescent vs 10W LED = 50W saved. At US grid 0.37kg/kWh = 18.5g/hour. UK grid = 10.5g/hour. Using US average.

sources.name: US DOE Energy Saver
sources.quote: LEDs use up to 90% less energy and last up to 25 times longer than traditional incandescent bulbs.

sources.name: Smarter House
sources.quote: A single 10-watt LED, used in place of a 43-watt halogen incandescent light bulb, will save about 800 kWh over its lifetime. That single replacement will eliminate emissions of 1000 pounds of carbon dioxide.

sources.name: Energy Use Calculator
sources.quote: A typical cheap (60 watt equivalent to incandescent) LED light bulb is advertised as providing 800 lumens, lasting up to 10,000 hours at 10 watts.

actions.action_name: Air drying clothes instead of tumble dryer
actions.calculation_notes: Tumble dryer uses ~4.5 kWh per load. At US grid 0.37kg/kWh = 1.67kg CO2. Rounded to 1700g.

sources.name: Energy Saving Trust UK
sources.quote: Tumble dryers are energy-intensive appliances using 4-5 kWh per cycle.

sources.name: Carbon Trust
sources.quote: Heating and drying processes are among the most energy-intensive household activities.

actions.action_name: Cold water laundry instead of hot
actions.calculation_notes: Hot wash uses ~1.6 kWh more than cold. At US grid = 592g. Rounded to 600g.

sources.name: Energy Saving Trust
sources.quote: Washing at 30°C instead of 40°C can save around 40% of the energy per wash cycle.

actions.calculation_notes: 7L/min flow, heating water from 13°C to 55°C. Energy calculation gives ~115g CO2 per minute.

sources.name: co2data.org
sources.quote: 89kg CO2 ÷ (25.7l × 0.59sw/p/d × 365d ÷ 7l/min) = 0.1154 kg CO2 per min

sources.name: Yarra Valley Water
sources.quote: Reduce an estimated 359 kg CO2-e emissions per annum. Assumes 7.1 minute down to 4 minute, 9 L/min flow rate.

sources.name: The Eco Guide
sources.quote: Heating 1 gallon of water produces, on average, 0.18 lbs of CO2. A five-minute shower creates 2.25lbs of CO2.

actions.action_name: Reusable shopping bag instead of plastic
actions.calculation_notes: Single-use plastic bag ~10-33g CO2. After breakeven uses (10-45 for PP bag), each use saves the full plastic bag emission.

sources.name: Danish EPA LCA 2018
sources.quote: Cotton bags need 7,100-20,000 uses to break even on all environmental indicators. Polypropylene bags break even in 10-45 uses.

sources.name: UK Environment Agency
sources.quote: HDPE bags have lower environmental impacts than paper or cotton bags when used once.

actions.action_name: Reusable water bottle instead of single-use plastic
actions.calculation_notes: Single-use 500ml PET bottle ~83g CO2e (production + transport). Reusable bottle breaks even in ~10-30 uses.

sources.name: Carbon Trust
sources.quote: Single-use plastic bottles have significant lifecycle emissions from production, filling, and transport.

actions.action_name: Buying secondhand clothing instead of new
actions.calculation_notes: Average new garment ~13kg CO2e. Secondhand extends life, avoiding new production.

sources.name: WRAP UK
sources.quote: Extending the life of clothes by just nine months reduces carbon, water and waste footprints by around 20-30% each.

actions.calculation_notes: Trees absorb 10-40kg CO2/year depending on species and climate. Conservative estimate: 15kg/year.

sources.name: EPA
sources.quote: Urban trees sequester 85-140 lbs CO2 over first 10 years.

actions.calculation_notes: Modern devices use ~1W standby (older up to 15W). At 1W × 24h = 24Wh × 0.37kg/kWh = 8.9g/day.

sources.name: Lawrence Berkeley National Lab
sources.quote: Modern regulations limit standby to ≤1W, down from 5-15W in older devices.

actions.calculation_notes: Transport accounts for only 5-6% of food emissions. Conservative transport-only savings.

sources.name: Our World in Data
sources.quote: Transport accounts for only 5-6% of food emissions globally. What you eat matters far more than where it comes from.

actions.calculation_notes: Dairy milk ~3.2kg CO2/L, oat milk ~0.9kg CO2/L. Per 250ml serving: 800g vs 225g = 575g saved. Conservative 460g.

sources.name: Our World in Data / Poore & Nemecek
sources.quote: Dairy milk has significantly higher emissions than plant-based alternatives across all environmental indicators.

actions.calculation_notes: Petrol car 164g/km vs EV ~50-70g/km (depending on grid). Savings ~100g/km on average grid.

sources.name: UK DEFRA 2024
sources.quote: Battery Electric Cars: Emissions for battery electric cars have decreased by 13.56%, driven by the penetration of newer, more efficient electric vehicles.

actions.calculation_notes: Two people sharing: 164g/2 = 82g each. Each additional passenger saves 82g/km vs solo driving.

sources.name: UK DEFRA 2024
sources.quote: Average car CO2 emissions divided by occupancy gives per-passenger rates.

actions.calculation_notes: Plastic straw weighs ~0.4g. Production emissions ~1-2g CO2e per straw.

sources.name: Environmental LCA studies
sources.quote: Single-use plastic items have small individual footprints but significant cumulative impact.

1.description: No Poverty - systemic issue, indirect actions

actions: ALL transport, food, energy, recycling actions

notes.regional_variation: Energy-related actions vary significantly by grid carbon intensity. US average 0.37 kg/kWh, UK 0.21 kg/kWh, France 0.05 kg/kWh. Consider allowing user input.
notes.food_caveat: Transport accounts for only 5-6% of food emissions. 'Eat local' has limited impact compared to 'eat less beef'.
notes.reusable_items_caveat: Cotton bags require 7,100+ uses to break even. Recommend polypropylene bags (10-45 uses breakeven).
notes.growing_vegetables_caveat: University of Michigan 2024 found urban agriculture has 6× higher emissions than conventional farming due to infrastructure. Exception: tomatoes grown outdoors vs greenhouse.
notes.flight_radiative_forcing: DEFRA uses 1.9× multiplier for non-CO2 aviation effects. Some scientists argue 2.7-3× is more accurate.
